hero.title: Temperature and humidity of every room at home, at a glance
hero.tagline: ESP32 + sensors · self-hosted · one container · open source, MIT

hardware.title: Hardware
hardware.intro: One small board per room, with two sensors that check each other:

step1.title: Start the server
step1.text: One container serves the upload API, the read API and this web app; the data directory must belong to uid 10001. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only: to let boards on the LAN reach it, uncomment the line with the server's LAN address in deploy/compose.yaml and run docker compose up -d again.
step1.code:
git clone https://github.com/lyu-huiyang/room-climate-monitor.git
cd room-climate-monitor/deploy
mkdir -p data && sudo chown 10001:10001 data
docker compose up -d --build

step2.title: Register a room
step2.text: The command prints the room's device key once; keep it for the next step.
step2.code: docker compose exec app rcm room add living-room --name "Living room"

step3.title: Flash the board
step3.text: Needs PlatformIO Core 6.2.0. Copy the example config, fill in Wi-Fi, the server's LAN address as SERVER_URL (for example http://192.168.1.10:8080), the room id and the device key, then build and flash.
step3.code:
cd ../firmware
cp include/secrets.example.h include/secrets.h
pio run -e supermini -t upload --upload-port <serial port>

why.title: Why self-hosted
why.home: Readings never leave your home network.
why.noCloud: No cloud service and no account.
why.oneFile: One SQLite file holds all the data; back it up with one command.
